draft.title: Population change
card: A place's population changes because of three things: births, deaths and migration. Migration is people moving into or out of the place.
births minus deaths. If more babies are born than people die, the population grows naturally. If deaths are higher, it falls.
people moving in minus people moving out. More arrivals than departures adds to the population. More departures than arrivals takes away from it.
Total population change = natural increase + net migration. Either part can be negative, so a place can grow even if deaths are higher than births, as long as enough people move in.
draft.remember: Population change = births minus deaths, plus people in minus people out.

a.q: A town has 300 births, 200 deaths, 500 people arriving and 100 people leaving in a year. What is its natural increase?
a.why: Natural increase is births minus deaths: 300 - 200 = 100. The 400 figure is net migration, which is a separate part of population change.
a.clue: Natural increase uses only births and deaths.

b.q: In one year, Coral Bay has 50 births, 80 deaths, 200 people arriving and 90 people leaving. What happens to its population?
b.why: Natural increase is 50 - 80 = -30. Net migration is 200 - 90 = 110. Adding them gives +80. The population still grows, because migration outweighs the natural decrease. Counting only births and deaths would wrongly suggest it falls.
b.clue: Work out both parts, then add them. Either part can be negative.

check.summary: No problems found. The card, both questions and both explanations correctly apply natural increase plus net migration: 100 for (a) and growth of 80 for (b).
